purpose: Defines the boundary between requirements documents (What) and design documents (How) and gives criteria to decide where content belongs, with severity catalog and gray-zone rules.
summary: Basic principles of requirements (What) versus design (How) documents
Relationship to ADRs: design states current design, ADR holds the rationale
First criterion: already-decided matters go to requirements, stated concretely
Main criterion: whether content belongs in the user manual
Category guide for quantitative targets, with no guarantee-style claims in design
Category guide for feature rationale and user value, which belongs only in requirements
Severity catalog for What/How boundary violations and type/diagram gray zones
Gray-zone allowances for data model types, diagrams, and quantitative targets
Lightweight traceability norms between design and requirement IDs, including additive development
tasks: Deciding whether content goes to requirements or design
Determining review finding severity for boundary violations
title: 要件定義書と設計書の境界ガイド
